newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. diplomat criticises Palestinians for torture.
newsitem.headline: U.S. diplomat criticises Palestinians for torture.

text.p: A U.S. diplomat criticised Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's self-rule Authority on Tuesday for torturing prisoners and failing to investigate corruption allegations.

Edward Abington, U.S. consul-general in East Jerusalem, was speaking to reporters in Ramallah after another U.S. official announced a six million dollar aid package for the Palestinian Legislative Council.

"Security is important but it can't come at the cost of human rights. Too many Palestinians have died while in Palestinian Authority custody. Those who break the law must be held accountable," said Abington, referring to a Palestinian who died during interrogation last month by Palestinian security forces.
"Faith in government is eroded by rumours of bribery and corruption that go uninvestigated," Abington added.
Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Meddein confirmed this week that Yousef Ismail Al-Baba, 32, was tortured to death and vowed to arrest the security officers involved.
Human rights groups have accused Palestinian security forces of systematically torturing prisoners and blamed the Palestinian Authority for not doing enough to halt the abuse.

According to the Washington-based Solidarity International for Human Rights group, 12 Palestinians have been tortured to death while under interrogation since the Palestinian Authority began taking control of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank in 1994 under interim peace deals with Israel.

Christopher Crowley, director of the United States Agency for Internationial Development (USAID), said the group would provide money to the Palestinian Legislative Council "to help it develop the tools necessary to function as a strong legislature".
